chunk-001:c002.proposition: God's necessarily good character grounds objective moral values, while divine commands consistent with that character constitute objective moral duties.

orphanFallback.rationale: This opening account independently advances the pro route by grounding value in God's character and obligation in commands expressing that character.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Godless normative realism is less plausible than theism because its independently real abstract moral objects add an extravagant ontology without sufficient support.

orphanFallback.rationale: As part of Craig's opening comparative case, the claim independently challenges the rival foundation's abstract ontology and contrasts it with grounding in a concrete God.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: The proposed causal connection between physical situations and abstract moral properties is obscure because abstract objects appear unable to enter causal relations with physical reality.

orphanFallback.rationale: The move independently presents a metaphysical objection to the natural-to-moral relation required by godless normative realism, even without a retained opposing move.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Defining obligation by decisive moral reasons mishandles supererogation, tends to require the morally best act, and supplies only a conditional reason to act morally rather than an unconditional duty.

orphanFallback.rationale: Craig presents these consequences as independent reasons that a reasons-based account fails to constitute the unconditional obligations at issue in the motion.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Physical causal closure and a self reduced to successive mental states eliminate free agency and an enduring moral agent, thereby undermining genuine accountability.

orphanFallback.rationale: The claim independently argues that the rival naturalistic framework lacks the persistent, causally efficacious agents required for praise, blame, and obligation.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Naturalism joined to unguided evolution undercuts confidence in reliable moral cognition, whereas theism can ground reliable cognitive faculties through divine supervision of evolution.

orphanFallback.rationale: The argument independently supplies the pro route's epistemic contrast: unguided selection favors adaptive behavior, while theism can account for truth-directed faculties.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c06.proposition: Divine commands can be the ultimate ground of duty within a hierarchy in which derivative moral principles and relevant circumstances determine obligations in particular cases.

orphanFallback.rationale: Even without an earlier retained objection, the hierarchy distinction constructively explains how general divine commands ground duties while promises and other derivative facts govern their application.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c07.proposition: Nonbelievers remain subject to divine moral requirements because people can intuitively apprehend the content and authority of moral law without identifying God as its source.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition constructively explains the universal scope of divine authority by distinguishing apprehension of a law's binding content from recognition of its lawgiver.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c08.proposition: General divine commands establish culpability, retributive responsibility, and divine judgment, while divine-command theory itself does not require the disputed premise that God has middle knowledge.

orphanFallback.rationale: Absent an earlier retained objection, the move still gives a positive purpose for general commands: they make wrongdoing accountable and provide a basis for retributive justice.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-08.proposition: God's nature is the paradigm and metric of moral goodness because God is conceived as the greatest conceivable and worship-worthy being whose goodness is essential.

orphanFallback.rationale: The paradigm account constructively supplies an internal standard of goodness rooted in God's essential nature rather than appealing to an external abstract moral metric.
